newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end higher, spot gold easier.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end higher, spot gold easier.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures settled higher across the board on Wednesday, as the dollar rose to around 113 yen after the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey, traders said.
The newly listed January contract ended at 1,360 yen. Other futures ranged from 10 yen to 13 yen per gram higher, with benchmark October ending up 10 yen at 1,348 yen.
Spot gold was easier at $374.55/85 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $374.70/5.20 in New York on Tuesday.
Private investors were liquidating their longs for most of the day, pressured by weak spot gold prices, while trade houses bought futures while selling spot gold in arbitrage.
Activity in the bullion market was quiet ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
"Although sporadic short-covering by funds was detected later in the day as the gold market was overwhelmingly short, sentiment remained bearish," one trader said.
Reports that Switzerland may change its constitution which currently requires gold holdings equivalent to about 40 percent of its currency in circulation did not affect the market, the traders said.
Platinum and silver futures were also higher in tandem with gold.
One trader said further gains in platinum futures could be limited as large long-positions still held by individual investors weighed on the market.
The benchmark October platinum contract was four yen higher at 1,371 yen, and the benchmark October silver contract was 1.6 yen per 10 grams higher at 176.7 yen.
The benchmark October palladium was up one yen at 422 yen after sluggish trade. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7431
